section_summary: This section combines Japanese wartime newspaper clippings, State Department translation-routing material, and press-monitoring reports on Japanese and Japanese-language media. Subjects include the Tripartite Pact, Japan’s military and economic mobilization, Japanese American evacuation, propaganda about the Pacific War and the “Greater East Asia” order, and the political outlook of Japanese communities in Argentina. The closing pages begin an Office of War Information transcript of Domei reports on Manchukuo’s heavy-industrial production.

subfiles.title: Dr. Ito Radiocasts on 1st Anniversary of 3-Power Treaty
subfiles.about: Reports Nobumi Ito’s anniversary broadcast presenting the Tripartite Pact as the foundation of Japanese diplomacy and a means of creating a new world order.
subfiles.summary: Dr. Ito's radiocast on the Tripartite Pact's first anniversary defends it as preventing wider war, lists later members, and says it remains the keynote of Japanese policy.

subfiles.title: Yamada Appointed New Defense Chief, War Office States
subfiles.about: Announces General Otozō Yamada’s appointment to command Japan’s new National Defense General Headquarters.
subfiles.summary: The War Office created a centralized command responsible directly to the emperor for the defense of Japan proper, Korea, Taiwan, and Karafuto. The article outlines the forces placed under Yamada and reviews his military career, including service in Central China and as Inspector-General of Military Education.

subfiles.title: Cabinet Approves Program for Labor
subfiles.about: Describes Cabinet approval of a wartime labor-mobilization program explained by Lieutenant-General Teiichi Suzuki.
subfiles.summary: Cabinet program directs labor to munitions, strategic industries, transport, agriculture and defense works, with temporary mobilization of men, women and students and new regulations contemplated.

subfiles.title: Perfection of Material Control
subfiles.about: Supports Imperial ordinances extending state control over materials, medical facilities, and transportation under the General Mobilization Law.
subfiles.summary: Editorial on the material-control ordinance: broad regulation of production through storage; Anglo-American pressure requires a planned economy, with accurate surveys, warehousing, supply routes and public cooperation.

subfiles.title: Translation Bureau Routing Note and Supporting Sheets
subfiles.from: J. Pritchard, Department of State Translating Bureau
subfiles.about: Advises that the Translating Bureau does not handle Japanese and suggests asking Mr. Van Valin to arrange translation of the attached material.
subfiles.summary: Pritchard states that Chinese and Japanese communications intended for the president are normally sent to Van Valin. The following pages are sparse Department of State communications, Far Eastern Affairs, and handwritten routing sheets associated with the request.

subfiles.title: Japanese Morning Press Digest of December 4, 1941
subfiles.about: Summarizes Tokyo morning-newspaper coverage of the Thailand crisis, domestic political measures, and Asian political and economic affairs.
subfiles.summary: Degraded Japanese morning press digest of December 4, 1941: interpretations of possible military entry into Thailand, the Diet term, Shanghai and Hong Kong, a princess's remains, and economic self-sufficiency and price controls.

subfiles.title: Summary of Japanese-Language Press, March 4–10, 1942
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Reviews Japanese American newspaper reactions to evacuation orders and the activities of the Japanese American Citizens’ League.
subfiles.summary: Press summary, March 4-10, 1942: loyalty and criticism of evacuation, concern for crops, Nisei views that blame lay with militarists, JACL's decision to cooperate and move to Salt Lake City, friction with the United Citizens Federation.

subfiles.title: Summary of Material Appearing in the Japanese-Language Press, March 25–April 11, 1942
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Surveys press coverage of curfew challenges, assembly centers, Manzanar, anti-Japanese sentiment in Colorado, and the survival of West Coast newspapers.
subfiles.summary: Press summary, March 25-April 11, 1942: Minoru Yasui's deliberate Portland curfew violation, Manzanar construction, a rejected Deming settlement, Manzanar self-government plans, hostility in southern Colorado, and newspaper plans during evacuation.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Continuation Page from the March 4–10 Japanese-Language Press Summary
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.about: Duplicates the report page concerning JACL policy, interorganizational disputes, and newspaper publication after evacuation.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate page of the March 4-10 summary: Saburo Kido's call for cooperation, JACL's move to Salt Lake City, disagreement with the United Citizens Federation, and subscription appeals.

subfiles.title: Translations from El Nichia Djidji, September 1–3, 1943
subfiles.to: Military and Naval Attachés, American Embassy, Buenos Aires; American Embassy, Santiago; Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Translates Japanese press claims concerning air operations in China and New Guinea and conditions in North China.
subfiles.summary: El Nichia Djidji, September 1-3, 1943: Japanese claims of attacks on American air bases and Allied losses near Salamaua, propaganda blaming a silk shortage for failed parachutes, and Japanese residents in North China.

subfiles.title: Translations from Diario Nan-A and El Argentin Djijo, September 1–15, 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, Second Secretary, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Military and Naval Attachés, American Embassy, Buenos Aires; American Embassy, Santiago; Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese-language Argentine press items from the first half of September 1943.
subfiles.summary: Diario Nan-A and El Argentin Djijo, September 1-15, 1943: Argentine nationalism, Axis claims, internees and exchange ships, Japanese residents in Peru and Argentina, Italy's surrender, censorship, with Warner's sarcastic comments.

subfiles.title: Translations from Diario Nan-A and El Argentin Djijo, September 16–30, 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, Second Secretary, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Military and Naval Attachés, American Embassy, Buenos Aires; American Embassy, Santiago; Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Reviews Japanese-language press commentary in Argentina during the second half of September 1943.
subfiles.summary: Items include Hanson Baldwin’s article on China, farewells to repatriating Japanese, criticism of American power and postwar planning, praise for Argentine neutrality, and reports on the Philippines and Ukraine. El Argentin Djijo’s editorials emphasize Japanese-Argentine friendship, Japanese language and character, shipping, and Argentina’s political future. The report also records Japanese community activities at Kyowa Park involving Attaché Kameda and Ambassador Tomii.

subfiles.title: Translations from Diario Nan-A and El Argentin Djijo, October 1–15, 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, Second Secretary, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Military and Naval Attachés, American Embassy, Buenos Aires; American Embassy, Santiago; Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Translates Japanese Argentine press material on Japanese loyalty, Argentine neutrality, Philippine independence, and wartime developments.
subfiles.summary: The report follows disputes among Buenos Aires Japanese editors, Diario Nan-A’s bilingual editorial policy, and its stated principles of loyalty to Japan alongside respect for Argentine law. It reproduces editorials on a supposed spiritual bond between Japan and Argentina and on Japanese-sponsored Philippine independence. Military claims from New Guinea and Bougainville, Japanese administrative measures, Argentine diplomatic appointments, and concern about American pressure on Argentine neutrality are also covered.

subfiles.title: Translations from El Nichia Djidji, November 5–8, 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, Second Secretary, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Santiago; Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese press claims about Pacific battles, mobilization, the Greater East Asia Conference, and Argentine Japanese community affairs.
subfiles.summary: El Nichia Djidji, November 5-8, 1943: claims of American losses around Rabaul and Bougainville, revised conscription, Philippine military expansion, rationing, the Greater East Asia Conference, and Buenos Aires community items.

subfiles.title: Translations from El Nichia Djidji, November 12–15, 1943
subfiles.from: Gerald Warner, Second Secretary, American Embassy, Buenos Aires
subfiles.to: Department of State; Office of Strategic Services
subfiles.about: Summarizes Japanese claims of major naval and air victories around Bougainville and related wartime items.
subfiles.summary: El Nichia Djidji, November 12-15, 1943: inflated claims of American fleet losses near Bougainville and Rabaul, a Hubei air attack, quinine gifts to the Philippines, a Singapore fisheries school, and Yamamoto's last exhortation.

subfiles.title: Outpost Report: Domei Press Service for the Pacific Zone, September 13–20, 1943
subfiles.doc_type: Office of War Information report and press transcript
subfiles.from: U.S. Office of War Information, New Delhi
subfiles.about: Introduces a confidential transcript of selected Domei Pacific Zone reports, beginning with a report on Manchukuo’s heavy industries.
subfiles.summary: OWI Outpost Report on Domei items, September 13-20, 1943: claimed Manchukuo production gains in iron, steel, metals, aluminum, synthetic gasoline and hydroelectric power under Five-Year Plans; continues.
